diagnoses.bug: After a zero-duration dispatch finishes inline, the loop advances to the next arrival instead of dispatching the next already-waiting customer at the same tick.
diagnoses.lesson: After processing an event that leaves a resource idle, immediately drain all eligible queued work before advancing the simulation clock.

diagnoses.bug: The code resets a preempted customer’s waiting budget and cumulative waited time, allowing repeated pauses to exceed patience and underreporting total wait.
diagnoses.lesson: Track cumulative resource budgets across interruptions; on each pause, subtract prior consumption and preserve accumulated totals when requeuing.

diagnoses.bug: The source violates the single-file interface by defining `main`, and it incorrectly returns `SignOnly` for a lone `-` instead of `InvalidDigit` because it treats any non-`+` first byte as magnitude.
diagnoses.lesson: Check interface constraints and distinguish allowed prefixes from disallowed characters before applying empty-payload error handling.

diagnoses.bug: The file defines `fn main()`, which violates the requirement to omit a main function.
diagnoses.lesson: Check source-level constraints explicitly, including forbidden entry points and attributes, before submitting code.

diagnoses.bug: The file defines `fn main()`, despite the requirement that the source contain no main function.
diagnoses.lesson: Check that generated source matches every required file-level constraint, including forbidden entry points and attributes.

diagnoses.bug: The file defines `fn main()`, contrary to the requirement that the source contain no main function.
diagnoses.lesson: Check that generated source matches every explicit interface and file-structure constraint, including required omissions.

diagnoses.bug: The parser reads base numbers before confirming the step operand is numeric, so malformed items such as `999999999999/` return NumberOverflow instead of InvalidSyntax at the item start.
diagnoses.lesson: Validate an input’s complete structural shape before interpreting its values, so malformed syntax takes precedence over value errors.

diagnoses.bug: `atom_value` classifies only all-digit strings or valid names, so an all-digit value that overflows `u32` reaches `InvalidSyntax` instead of `NumberOverflow`.
diagnoses.lesson: Classify numeric tokens before validating their values, so overflow and bounds errors retain the required precedence over syntax errors.

diagnoses.bug: Path validation reports an earlier component-format error before checking whether a later byte is NUL, but NUL must take precedence anywhere in the path.
diagnoses.lesson: When requirements specify global validation precedence, complete the higher-priority scan before returning errors from local checks.

diagnoses.bug: The rounded square-root calculation multiplies `d2` by 1,000,000 in `u128`, which can overflow for unrestricted i64 inputs before range validation rejects them.
diagnoses.lesson: Prove intermediate arithmetic fits its type across every accepted execution path, including inputs validated only after a calculation.

diagnoses.bug: The rounding helper’s binary-search upper bound and intermediate products are safe only for the specified coordinate range, so malformed i64 extremes can overflow before rejection if used outside validated paths.
diagnoses.lesson: Validate numeric inputs before arithmetic, and prove intermediate bounds for every operation on all values the public interface can receive.

diagnoses.bug: The parser accumulates arbitrarily long digit sequences in `u128` with unchecked arithmetic, so debug builds can panic and release builds can wrap before reporting the required `OutOfRange` error.
diagnoses.lesson: When parsing unbounded numeric input, detect range overflow during digit accumulation instead of relying on a wider integer type to hold the entire token.

diagnoses.bug: When the numerator starts with a non-digit other than `-`, parsing returns InvalidByte at offset 0 without validating the remaining bytes, so a later missing required digit can be misreported.
diagnoses.lesson: Validate the complete input grammar before returning syntax errors so the reported failure reflects the earliest invalid byte or missing required token.

diagnoses.bug: The parser reports a missing numerator digit immediately after a leading minus before checking the rest of the input, so syntax errors later in the text can incorrectly lose to an earlier end-of-token error.
diagnoses.lesson: Validate the complete input grammar before returning any syntax error whose position depends on reaching the end of a token.

diagnoses.bug: Solve builds the basis with a shape derived by dividing its data length by the variable count, so when there are zero variables and free columns the required n×f shape is lost; it also fails to construct the specified identity basis for equations with no variables.
diagnoses.lesson: Preserve explicit dimensions independently of storage length, especially for empty matrices; derive output shapes from the specification, not from element counts.

diagnoses.bug: Both parsers reject a trailing slash before validating preceding segments, so a path such as /%GG/ reports the slash offset instead of the earlier invalid escape.
diagnoses.lesson: When validation rules specify an order, validate each component in that order before checking whole-input constraints that occur later.

diagnoses.bug: The wildcard final-segment check is a stub that always returns true, so patterns with a non-final wildcard are incorrectly accepted.
diagnoses.lesson: Turn every validation requirement into an explicit check, and verify that placeholder helpers enforce the stated condition before relying on them.

diagnoses.bug: A zero-tail wildcard route builds an extra slash because the loop emits its separator even when the wildcard value is empty, so the generated path does not represent zero consumed segments.
diagnoses.lesson: When serializing optional or empty collections, verify that delimiters are emitted only between actual elements, not before an empty collection.

diagnoses.bug: decode_group infers padding from zero-valued digits, so valid groups containing A in position two or three lose decoded bytes.
diagnoses.lesson: Represent syntax explicitly instead of inferring it from data values; valid data may share a value with a control-state sentinel.

diagnoses.bug: Width reduction always chooses the rightmost column wider than one, instead of the currently widest eligible column with rightmost tie-breaking.
diagnoses.lesson: When an algorithm specifies repeated selection, implement its full ranking rule before applying each step; tie-breaking alone is not the selection rule.

diagnoses.bug: The hyphen acceptance comparison squares `unused` and adds `hyphen_cost` without accounting for overflow, so the cost penalty can wrap and incorrectly accept an opportunity.
diagnoses.lesson: Before arithmetic used in a decision, prove its range is bounded or use checked operations so overflow cannot change the result.

diagnoses.bug: The code expands each expression immediately after parsing it, so an earlier value error can be returned before a later syntax error is scanned.
diagnoses.lesson: Separate whole-input validation from evaluation when error precedence requires later structural errors to outrank earlier runtime failures.

lessons: Validate the complete input structure and grammar before interpreting values or returning errors; honor specified global validation precedence.
Validate inputs before arithmetic, and prove every intermediate fits across all accepted execution paths; use checked operations when needed.
Check every explicit interface, file, and source constraint, including required omissions and forbidden constructs, before submitting.
Implement each algorithm’s complete selection and tie-breaking rule at every step.
After each event that makes a resource available, process all eligible queued work before advancing time; preserve cumulative budgets across interruptions and requeues.
Preserve explicit dimensions and represent control state separately from valid data values.
When serializing collections, emit delimiters only between actual elements.
Detect numeric overflow during digit accumulation instead of relying on a wider type to hold an unbounded token.
